draft.title: Surface area of a sphere
card: A sphere is a perfectly round solid. Every point on its surface is the same distance, the radius \(r\), from its centre.
The surface area of a sphere is \(A = 4\pi r^{2}\). Square the radius first, then multiply by \(4\pi\).
A hemisphere is half a sphere. Its curved surface is half of \(4\pi r^{2}\), which is \(2\pi r^{2}\).
A ball has radius 5 cm. \(A = 4 \times \pi \times 5^{2} = 100\pi\), which is about \(314.2\) cm\(^{2}\). Area is measured in square units.
draft.remember: Sphere: \(4\pi r^{2}\). Curved surface of a hemisphere: half of that.

a.q: A sphere has radius 3 cm. What is its surface area, to 1 decimal place?
a.why: \(A = 4\pi r^{2} = 4 \times \pi \times 3^{2} = 36\pi\), which is about \(113.1\) cm\(^{2}\). The option \(37.7\) comes from using \(4\pi \times 3\), which forgets to square the radius.
a.clue: Square the radius before multiplying by \(4\pi\).

b.q: A dome on a building is a hemisphere with radius 10 m. Its curved roof is to be painted. What area needs paint, to the nearest square metre?
b.why: The curved surface of a hemisphere is \(2\pi r^{2} = 2 \times \pi \times 10^{2} = 200\pi\), which is about \(628\) m\(^{2}\). The option \(1257\) is the whole sphere, which is twice as much as the dome's curved roof.
b.clue: Only half of the sphere's surface is the roof.
